Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

nbzinbreg 0.0.0.9000

  • NMES1988 data analysis (inst/benchmark/nmes_functions.R):

    • Poisson regression (glm()), nbreg() and zinbreg() fits, with a sensitivity fit that adds health to the zero part;
    • the descriptive evidence, kept apart from the model comparison: one Poisson with the sample mean gives 13.7 zeros, the fitted Poisson regression 46.7, NB 608.0 and ZINB 708.9, against 683 observed;
    • incidence rate ratios and structural-zero odds ratios with Wald intervals, theta with Wald and profile intervals, and rootograms;
    • a parametric bootstrap LR test of NB against ZINB (inst/benchmark/nmes_bootstrap.R), run in checkpointed chunks that resume exactly after an interruption, with the run status (COMPLETE / FAILED) kept apart from the inference (CONCLUSIVE / INCONCLUSIVE).

    The results of record (B = 999: COMPLETE and CONCLUSIVE, p = 0.001 with failure bounds 0.001 to 0.033) are saved with the package and used by the report.

  • The prohibited-call detector in the tests also catches function names built at run time and functions taken out of a namespace by name.

  • Simulation study of zinbreg() (inst/benchmark/simulation.R):

    • the setup: 1000 data sets of n = 500 from a known ZINB model (two covariates per part, fixed design), fitted with zinbreg();
    • every fit is classified (usable, boundary, invalid, not converged, error) with a reason;
    • the summaries: bias, relative bias, Monte Carlo SD against the mean reported SE, RMSE and Wald coverage, each with a Monte Carlo SE (analytic or bootstrap over the replications);
    • profile-interval coverage for theta on 200 data sets.

    The results of record (all 1000 fits usable, coverage 94.5% to 95.8%) are saved with the package and used by the report.

  • Benchmark against MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl() on bioChemists and NMES1988 (inst/benchmark/):

    • validity checks for every pair, and side-by-side tables against the required tolerances;
    • supplementary comparisons (SE(theta), SE(log theta), the numeric Hessian);
    • bench::mark() timings;
    • a code fingerprint that ties the results to the installed code.

    Every required quantity is within its tolerance. The results of record are saved with the package and used by the report.

  • nbreg() fits negative binomial (NB2) regression by IRLS for the coefficients alternated with Newton-Raphson for theta, with backtracking line searches and no general-purpose optimizer. At default settings it matches MASS::glm.nb() within the required tolerances.

  • nbreg_control() validates every setting; nbreg() revalidates control objects edited after creation.

  • zinbreg() fits zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM, with a logistic IRLS M-step for the zero part and nbreg()’s algorithm, with weights 1 - tau, for the count part. No general-purpose optimizer is used. Two-part formulas y ~ x | z are supported, with offsets in either part, weights, subset and na.action. At default settings it matches pscl::zeroinfl() within the required tolerances on bioChemists and NMES1988.

  • EM is checked at every iteration: the log-likelihood never decreases, neither M-step lowers its part of the EM objective, and every M-step flag is recorded. EM stops only when the changes are small and a gradient check passes (Newton decrement of the analytic gradient and Hessian at most grad_tol). A fit is reported as converged only if, in addition, the final M-steps converged and no violation occurred.

  • Coefficients without a finite estimate are detected per part and explained: a zero-part group without zeros, a group whose counts are all zero, other drift, or no zero inflation at all. Their standard errors are NA.

  • Standard errors come from the analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood in (count, zero, log theta), or optionally the numeric one (zinbreg_control(hessian = "numeric")). Both are validated before inversion.

  • zinbreg_control() validates every setting, including starting values, and resolve_control() revalidates edited control objects for both models.

  • Methods for zinbreg fits: print(), summary() (count and zero tables, with a Log(theta) row), coef() and vcov() (with model = "full", "count" or "zero" and pscl’s names), logLik(), fitted(), residuals(), nobs() and predict(). predict() has types "response", "count", "zero" and "prob", with newdata, delta-method se.fit and offsets. For "prob", at may be in any order, and a result over 1e7 cells is refused.

  • All inputs are checked; problems raise classed errors (nbzinbreg_error_input, _rank, _fit) and classed warnings (nbzinbreg_warning_convergence, _monotone, _theta, _divergence, _se).

  • Methods for nbreg fits: print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), logLik(), fitted(), residuals(), nobs() and predict() (with newdata, se.fit and offsets).

  • confint() for both classes: Wald intervals for the coefficients, and a profile-likelihood interval for theta found by bisection on log(theta) without a root finder. Every endpoint has a status (finite, a certified unbounded limit, or unresolved at a bound), and a profile value above the fit’s maximum stops with an error.

  • anova() for nested nbreg fits and for nested zinbreg fits. Nesting is checked on the model matrices, each larger fit is verified by an embedding refit, and chi-squared p-values are given only for regular fits.

  • overdispersion_test(): Poisson against NB, with the boundary-corrected p-value and a certified Poisson limit when theta is on its upper bound.

  • vuong_test(): the Vuong statistics as in pscl::vuong() (descriptive only, because NB is the boundary pi = 0 of ZINB), and an optional parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of NB against ZINB.

    • It uses the closure supremum of the ZINB likelihood and boundary-aware replicates.
    • Its p-value comes with bounds for failed replicates, and the test is declared inconclusive when they could change the decision.

  • simulate() methods and boot_se(), parametric bootstrap standard errors.

    • Frequency weights are honoured (w independent draws per row).
    • Boundary replicates are kept, per parameter.
    • Failed replicates are counted, with a warning up to 10% and an error above.

  • expected_counts() and rootogram(): observed against expected count frequencies with a grouped tail row, and a hanging rootogram.

  • tidy() and glance() for both classes.

  • zinbreg() now detects complete separation of the zero part by a continuous covariate. Extreme fitted probabilities are confirmed by a likelihood certificate, so a well-identified zero part with extreme probabilities is not misreported.

  • New warning class nbzinbreg_warning_bootstrap.
